subject: literature
passage: The water of the mountain lake was so cold that Matteo's toes ached the moment he stepped in. All he wanted was to run back to the warm towel he had left on the shore. ______ he had promised his older sister that he would swim out to the wooden raft before the summer ended, so he took a deep breath and waded in up to his waist.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

explanation.why: The first two sentences say the water was painfully cold and Matteo wanted to leave. The last sentence says he went into the water anyway because of a promise. A transition that shows he acted in spite of what was just described is needed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. His promise is not an example of wanting to run back to the shore; it works against that wish.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Similarly" signals a matching idea, but wading in is the opposite of running back to the towel.
explanation.C: Correct. "Even so" shows that Matteo waded in despite the cold and his wish to return to his towel.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The cold water and Matteo's wish to leave did not cause him to wade in; he waded in despite them.
